response.markdown_report:
**Synthesis and insights.**

Three starting-point insights guide this early-stage proposal. First, training-position margins may describe a different task from appended-mask prediction. Diagnostic conclusions therefore require agreement with deployed BERT4Rec scoring.

Second, broad relevance versus immediate choice is the reported failure mode. Histories alone cannot establish compatibility, ownership, or present intent, so sensitivity measurements must remain behavioral descriptions.

Third, unavailable category metadata and empty samples weaken existing probes. Empty observations should return null with counts, while unavailable metadata should remain explicitly unavailable.

Three literature insights refine the approach. BERT4Rec learns through masked-item prediction [1]. Probes must preserve its reserved mask and prevent target leakage.

History-removal research finds accuracy sensitive to trailing training interactions [2]. This motivates matched recent/older inference perturbations, but does not establish their effects in advance.

Negative sampling influences evaluation reliability [3]. Diagnostic candidate sets must therefore remain fixed, and stress-test results must stay separate from selection HR@10.

**Directions and framework.**

| Direction | Question | Evidence | Boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Task correctness | Does diagnosis reproduce serving? | Predictor score agreement; mask checks | Engineering validity |
| Temporal specificity | Which history positions affect ranking? | Paired deletion and swap effects | Sensitivity, not intent |
| Measurement coverage | Where are conclusions supported? | Counts, missingness, popularity strata | No invented attributes |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Serving-aligned paired sensitivity probe: 5/8/3.** Originality: combines established checks and interventions, but introduces no new backbone. Potential: supports interpretable iteration, although sensitivity may not predict HR@10. Difficulty: reuses inference, but requires exact export parity [1,2].
2. **Recency-weighted masked-target loss: 3/7/3.** Originality: a simple weighting adaptation, but familiar. Potential: may emphasize current interests, although useful older evidence may suffer. Difficulty: small loss change, but requires budgeted training comparisons [1,2].
3. **Popularity-stratified margin audit: 3/6/2.** Originality: applies established stratification, but adds little methodological novelty. Potential: can reveal aggregate blind spots, although small strata are noisy. Difficulty: uses training counts, but requires careful denominators [3].

**Selected idea: serving-aligned paired sensitivity diagnostics.** At 0% progress, establish trustworthy measurements before changing training. Freeze each category’s single BERT4Rec checkpoint. On training-only prefixes, retain the same target and candidates while deleting equal numbers of recent or older interactions, or swapping adjacent history items. Append MASK after each retained history, preserve left padding, and gather its actual final nonpadding index.

Report paired target-rank changes, reciprocal-rank changes, top-10 overlap, valid counts, and user-bootstrap intervals. First verify diagnostic/exported score agreement. Preserve `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)`, `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)`, and `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt`; return measured metrics with definitions and nulls for unavailable observations. These diagnostics cannot substitute for pinned macro validation HR@10 or justify inferred intent.

References: [1] [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690); [2] [Betello et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.13165); [3] [Sampling reliability](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086).

idea.description: Add serving-aligned, paired history-sensitivity diagnostics to the corrected BERT4Rec baseline, retaining one trained model per category and all host compatibility interfaces.
idea.motivation: Existing training-position margins do not verify appended-mask serving behavior. The qualitative diagnosis suggests insufficient specificity and recency sensitivity, but supplies no measured evidence that a particular architectural change will help. An inference-aligned probe provides an inexpensive basis for subsequent controlled trials.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Do not change training in this initial diagnostic proposal. Use only training-history prefixes for additional probes; construct targets outside the input prefix and exclude padding/mask IDs from candidates. Freeze candidates across paired variants. For each variant, truncate history to leave mask capacity, append the reserved MASK, left-pad, and select the actual final nonpadding index. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, and predict_score(features, items); compare their scores with the embedded predictor before interpreting results. Keep original masked-position margin probes only where the family-specific sample_batch confirms valid masked supervision. Restore model training/evaluation state after probing. Return metrics and metric_definitions, including sample counts, candidate construction, perturbation sizes, and nulls when observations are absent. Keep category breakdowns empty because item category metadata is unavailable. Bootstrap users within category for diagnostic intervals. Do not combine diagnostic scores with neural predictions, and do not treat simulator abstention or unknown identity as negative labels. Selection remains the host's unchanged macro validation HR@10; diagnostics provide no claimed accuracy improvement.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    remember model.training; set model.eval()
    verify reserved MASK != PAD and MASK outside real catalog
    verify masked-supervision contract on sampled loader batches
    examples = deterministic training-prefix examples(seed=42)
    for example in examples:
        history, target, fixed_candidates = example
        k = min(configured_k, floor((len(history)-1)/2))
        if k < 1: record insufficient-history count; continue
        variants = {original: history,
                    recent_removed: history[:-k],
                    older_removed: history[k:],
                    local_swap: deterministic_adjacent_swap(history)}
        for name, variant in variants:
            sequence = left_pad(tail(variant, maxlen-1) + [MASK])
            index = max(position where sequence[position] != PAD)
            features = view.log2feats(sequence)[index]
            scores = view.predict_score(features, fixed_candidates)
            assert finite(scores)
            record target rank, reciprocal rank, top10 IDs
        verify original scores match exported predictor within tolerance
        record paired differences and top10 overlap
    aggregate by category with counts and paired user-bootstrap intervals
    restore previous model state
    return {metrics: measured_results, metric_definitions: explicit_definitions}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    embed measured metrics and definitions
    request evidence-linked findings; distinguish missingness, sensitivity,
    serving defects, and hypotheses requiring validation

originality.positive: Unifies serving parity, matched perturbations, and missingness-aware reporting within the required BERT4Rec diagnostic interface.
originality.negative: The individual methods are established engineering checks and sensitivity analyses rather than a new recommendation model.

future_potential.positive: Can support reliable subsequent experiments on masking, recency weighting, and representation capacity without changing evaluation conditions.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic sensitivity may not correlate with validation HR@10 and cannot establish users' immediate needs.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the trained model and existing scoring interfaces without additional training or independent predictors.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires careful mask placement, fixed candidates, deterministic perturbations, exported-predictor parity, and correct user-level aggregation.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item modeling for sequential recommendation.
Provides the basis for mask-aligned training and serving diagnostics.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed diagnostic suite or its relationship to this benchmark's HR@10.
Masked-item modeling alone does not establish compatibility or immediate purchase intent.

related_work.title: Betello et al.: Sequential recommendation history-removal study
contributions: Reports stronger accuracy effects from removing trailing training interactions than beginning or middle interactions.
limitations: Training-data removal findings do not directly establish inference-perturbation effects for BERT4Rec.
Position sensitivity does not demonstrate causal effects on personal intent.

related_work.title: Sampling reliability in recommendation evaluation, RecSys 2025
contributions: Examines how negative sampling affects evaluation reliability and agreement with full evaluation.
Supports fixing candidates during paired comparisons.
limitations: Does not validate training-prefix diagnostics as predictors of the pinned benchmark's validation performance.
Sampled and full-catalog results describe different candidate conditions.
